defect.description: The setting is read as settings['FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE'] or False instead of settings.getbool(...): command-line overrides arrive as text, so -s FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE=False (or =0) gives the non-empty string 'False', which is truthy and turns active mode on.

review_items: feedstorage.py:27 — `or False` makes the string 'False' from the command line truthy, enabling active mode
test_feedstorage.py:16-18 — tests pass Python True and never exercise the command-line string path
feedstorage.py:27 — use settings.getbool instead of the raw value with `or False` (nit)
feedstorage.py:31-38 — FTP connection not in a with block, leaks on error (pre-existing)
votes.evidence_quote: When `from_command_line` supplies `-s FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE=False`, the value is the string `"False"`. The expression `"False" or False` evaluates to `"False"` (a non-empty string, which is truthy), so `self.active` becomes truthy and `ftp.set_pasv(False)` fires on line 34 — the opposite of what the user requested.
votes.justification: The first finding names the same cause and behaviour at from_settings: the raw read with `or False` lets the command-line string 'False' stay truthy, which turns active mode on. The nit recommends getbool as the fix for the same defect.
